about: Arena's motion per verb, measured in the gameplay recordings in ~/Movies/arena (indexed in ~/arena) for docs/engine-architecture.md, K27. The verbs are data/ui-conventions.json's. These are reference: a verb's values there are what the stage plays, and `by motion` prints these beside them. `just conventions` derives each verb's summary here from its instances.

Each instance names its recording, the clip's start and span, its crop in the recording's pixels (1920x1080; SN9QFe2kM4Y is 2560x1440), and how it was taken: `tracker` is `just video measure`, which follows one moving card; `filmstrip` counts frames of `just video film` at the recording's frame rate (30 fps, 60 for UrGalw_f35w and SN9QFe2kM4Y), with `why` the tracker was not used. Its `command` retakes it.

duration_ms runs from the first frame of change to the first frame at rest; delay_ms from the instant `since` names; stagger_ms between like motions of one batch, start to start; peak is the largest size over the size at rest; curve is one of linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, or none where nothing travels. A number not taken is null. Filmstrip numbers are good to a frame at the rate filmed, and the coarser strips' to about 100 ms.

start is the size where the motion begins over the size at rest, null where not taken; emerge's are read by eye from the first frame its copy shows (about +-30%, as each note says). `by motion` (tools/src/beryl_tools/motion.py) prints a verb's summary here beside what a capture of Beryl's stage measures, as reference, with no verdict.

A summary is the median and range of each number over all the verb's instances, the commonest curve, and the same per case when there are several. Where a verb's cases differ (fly's draw, vanish's finished ability), the case's own summary is the reference.

To retake an instance, run its command, edit its numbers here and run `just conventions`. Instances were taken by agents with the arena-video skill; one of each verb was checked by eye (by-w8gv.21.18).
